requirement: When the setup advisory of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook` also applies, the hook MUST provide the sentence of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` and the advisory together in one agent context, with the sentence first.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.setup_state` has one clause: "the hook MUST provide the sentence of `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` and the advisory together in one agent context, with the sentence first." It states only what the hook outputs. The output has to be a single agent context, and the skill sentence has to come before the setup advisory. A reviewer can check both by looking at the hook's output.

I considered whether "one agent context" prescribes a structure, such as a particular type, signature, library or named interface. It does not. Any implementation that emits the sentence and the advisory in one context, sentence first, satisfies it. That includes one that builds a single string, one that joins parts, or one that uses a different helper layout. An implementation that built the two pieces differently but produced the same single ordered context would behave the same and still conform. The text does not say which type carries the context, which function builds it, or how the two pieces are composed. Those choices are discretionary.

The cited requirements `requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook` and `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` only supply context. They define the advisory and the sentence. They are not obligations of this requirement. No implementation roots were supplied, so no structural obligation needs implementation evidence here. Whether the output is combined and ordered correctly is behavioral, and the behavioral criterion covers it.

behavioral: The requirement has one behavioral obligation. When the setup advisory applies, the hook MUST provide the skill sentence and the advisory together in one agent context, with the sentence first.

`tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_puts_the_skill_sentence_before_the_setup_advisory]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement and covers it:
- It sets up a project that lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]` and has no `md/habeas.css`. It asserts the CSS file is absent, so the advisory applies.
- It runs the real `habeas hook session-start` binary through the `session_start` helper.
- It asserts that the `SessionStart` object has exactly one key. That is the single `additionalContext`, which matches "one agent context".
- It asserts that the context starts with the independently defined `SKILL_SENTENCE` constant, which gives "sentence first".
- It asserts that the remainder starts with "Habeas Codicem is not fully configured" and contains "habeas setup", which shows the advisory is in the same context.
- It asserts that exactly one sentence points to the `habeas` skill.

A hook that put the advisory first, split the output into separate contexts, or dropped either part would fail these assertions.

`tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py#def[main]` is an end-to-end check through Symposium. Its `{test}` markers sit on the incomplete-setup step. It asserts that the delivered context starts with the skill sentence and contains the advisory. It also asserts that once setup is complete only the skill sentence is delivered. This adds evidence to the Rust test.

The example `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.incomplete_setup` matches the same scenario. I found no unchecked obligation and no ambiguity.

text: When the setup advisory of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook` also applies, the hook MUST provide the sentence of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` and the advisory together in one agent context, with the sentence first.

For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive a Symposium `SessionStart` hook. The hook MUST check whether the configuration and files required by `requirements.cli.setup`, {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.setup`, and {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.setup.configuration` are present and compatible. If not, it MUST provide nonblocking agent context saying that Habeas Codicem is not fully configured and suggesting `habeas setup`. If setup is complete or no applicable project is found, it MUST provide no setup advisory. The hook MUST NOT modify project files or run setup itself.

For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. That context MUST contain exactly one sentence that points to the skill. The sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill of {cite}`requirements.cli.overview_skill` before starting any work in the project.

In a project that lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]` but has no `habeas.css` in its book source directory, the agent context starts with the skill sentence, followed by the advisory saying Habeas Codicem is not fully configured and suggesting `habeas setup`. {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.setup_state`
